Self.Wiki: An AI destination point: a spot that enemy AI looks for and moves to, such as a snipe position, a piece of cover or a firing position against a set target. AI logic scripts find points with SearchAiDestinationPoint (by Point Type, within a radius of the AI), SearchAiDestinationPointEx and SearchAiDestinationPointShoot, then claim one with ReserveAiDestinationPoint. A reserved point is skipped by every other search until it is released, so two enemies don't take the same spot. Only the region's position is used. Change Area Enable State (2003[1008]) on the region's Entity ID turns the point off, and searches skip it. Retail: 643 points in 23 mission maps.

AiTarget_UnkT00.Wiki: What the point is for. A search finds the point when it asks for this type or for Secondary Point Type. Snipe and Cover are what the shared AI scripts search for; Shoot points also need Shoot Target Entity ID. Shield, Defence and Search are defined for the AI scripts but no retail point uses them. Retail: Cover 356, Shoot 183, Snipe 104.

AiTarget_UnkT01.Wiki: A second type the point also counts as, read the same way as Point Type. Set it to the same value as Point Type for a single-type point. 0 is Snipe, not 'none': 13 retail Cover points have 0 here, so they are also snipe points. Retail: equal to Point Type on 630 of 643 points.

AiTarget_UnkT04.Wiki: Only used when the point is a Shoot point. The entity ID of the character the point is for: SearchAiDestinationPointShoot only finds Shoot points whose entity matches the target the AI is searching against. A short ID (below 10000) in a mission map is read as that map's own entity, the same way event scripts read it. 0 on every other point. Retail: every Shoot point names an enemy of its own map (700, 870 to 875).
